 Versus

 About 30 Years, R/o Khariyawas, Kuchera, Nagaur.
 ----Respondents
 For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Vishal Sharma.

For Respondent(s) : Mr. Vikram Rajpurohit, P.P.
 Mr. Hanuman Prajapat, Aga.

Mr. Mayank Khatri, for R/2  (complainant)
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ARUN MONGA Order (Oral) 10/10/2024 1.

Quashing of an FIR No.095/2024 dated 01.04.2024lodged at Police Station Degana, District Nagaur, for offences under Sections376 and 384 of IPC and all consequential proceedings pursuant thereto, is sought herein.

2. Briefly relevant facts of the case are that Private Respondent No.2 approached Police Station Degana, District Nagaur, alleging that in January 2022, the petitioner video called her on Instagram, which she was using under the name of Kritika Dudi.
She declined to talk to the petitioner and informed him that she was a married woman, asking him not to call her again.
However, the petitioner recorded the screenshot and started blackmail her, threatening to viral the video of the screen recording.
Subsequently, petitioner forced the complainant to agree to meet him on October 25, 2023, at Mehrana Bus Stand.
The petitioner assured her that he would delete the screen recording if she met him.
They both went to a hotel where she provided her I.D. at the hotel room.
Petitioner gave a drink to her and when she got intoxicated, he allegedly raped her and also took naked pictures to blackmail her.

sentences.text: Based on these allegations, an FIR was registered against the petitioner under Sections 376 and 384 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
3. In the aforesaid backdrop, I have heard learned counsel for the respective parties and have perused the case file.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner states that both the petitioner and the prosecutrix were no doubt already married but their relationship was consensual; therefore, the ingredients of Section 376 IPC are not made out.
The FIR was registered due to a misunderstanding, which resulted in an acrimonious altercation.
5. Learned counsel for the respondent No.2/prosecutrix also agrees with the aforesaid submission made by learned counsel for the petitioner.

He states that the prosecutrix now deeply regrets taking the extreme step of making the allegation under Section 376 IPC against the petitioner-accused,
with whom she had a serious discord at the relevant time, and she falsely implicated him despite their consensual relationship.

5.1 Subsequently, the prosecutrix realized the gravity of her mistake,
and has arrived at an amicable compromise dated 10.05.2024 (reduced in writing) with the petitioner of her own [2024:RJ-JD:41667] (3of 3) [CRLMP-2712/2024] free will, without any coercion or duress.
She does not wish to press charges against the petitioner and proceed further in the matter.
As for both of them being married, he submits that the offence, at worst, is that of bigamy, which is not the subject matter of the present FIR.
7. Learned counsel for petitioner and respondent No.2 place reliance on a decision of Supreme Court in the case of Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab & Anr. [(2012) 10 SCC 303].

entities.text: Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab & Anr. [(2012) 10 SCC 303]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: They urge that the impugned FIR and all consequential proceedings may be quashed.
8. On Court query, learned counsel for the respondent No.2- complainant and learned Public Prosecutor, they have no objection if the FIR in question is quashed.
9. Accordingly, the present misc. petition is allowed.
FIR No.095/2024 dated 01.04.2024lodged at Police Station Degana, District Nagaur, for offences under Sections376 and 384 of IPC, and all consequential proceedings pursuant thereto,
are hereby quashed.
10. Pending application(s), if any, also stand disposed of.

(ARUN MONGA),J 114-Sumit/-
